clue.text: Airlines flying over the capital of an island

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lie over, covering, the word the on both sides
letters sent flying are scattered, so the word airlines is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Planes flying in above the main town of some island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering on both sides, so the rearranged letters wrap round the word. St Helier is the capital of Jersey in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helier is the chief town and seat of government of Jersey, a Channel Island.

clue.text: Cocktail served as 'cider'

indicators.note: a drink served up is turned out in a new form, so the letters of as and cider are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mixed drink is passed off as cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' is the anagram signal: AS plus CIDER rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Basic dwelling with one good toilet

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A simple house that comes with a single decent lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a simple dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of snow.

clue.text: Asian island is encapsulated by order and loyalty among people

indicators.note: something encapsulated is enclosed in a capsule, so the island and the letter sit inside the word for order

parts.note: trim means good order or condition, as in 'in fine trim'
Bali is an island of Indonesia
is shortens to 's, giving the single letter

explanation.surface: An Asian island is somehow wrapped in order and a sense of community loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' here is the noun as in 'in good trim', not a command; 'is' is shortened to 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong loyalty to one's own group or tribe, the definition's loyalty among a people.

clue.text: Bird about to go north, then north-east

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word for about is reversed

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bird flies north and then veers north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to go north' means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword staple among birds.

clue.text: It comes out about right, resulting in a chilling disturbance

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the rearranged letters go round the letter for right
letters put out of order are disarranged, so it comes is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something emerges that is just right, causing a chilly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IT COMES into ICESTOM, and 'about' puts that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice storm is freezing rain that coats everything in ice, a literally chilling weather disturbance.

clue.text: Direct official accompanying the Queen

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a sports official
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A senior official is in attendance on Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone is to direct them elsewhere, as to a specialist or a source.

clue.text: Perfectionist rejected best stuff from time to time

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: tops is informal for the best

indicators.note: taking only some of the letters now and then, here the odd letters of stuff

explanation.surface: A perfectionist turned down the finest material every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' picks SUF from STUFF; TOPS plus SUF, 'rejected', reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone who fusses over details, a nitpicking perfectionist.

clue.text: Layer of paint that is soft at the edges and faded in the extreme

parts.note: a wash is a thin coat of paint or colour
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: only the edge letters of soft are taken, its first and last

explanation.surface: A coat of paint that has softened round the borders and has badly faded.
explanation.definitionFit: Washy means pale or faded, so the superlative is the most faded, faded to the extreme.

clue.text: Flirtatious relationship ultimately destroyed marriage

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of destroyed

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance between two people or families

explanation.surface: A flirtation in the end wrecked a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic or flirtatious affair.

clue.text: Oil companies finally accepting international sanctions

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the letter for international goes inside

parts.note: fat, like oil, is a grease used in cooking

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of companies

explanation.surface: Oil firms at last bow to sanctions from an international body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil companies' looks like one idea, but Oil gives FAT and 'companies finally' S; 'accepting' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiats are authoritative decrees or orders, so sanctions in the sense of official authorisations.

clue.text: Clubs said to embrace hard type of music

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the letter for hard goes between

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
oral means spoken or said
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Nightclubs reportedly take up hardcore music.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir, a kind or genre of music.

clue.text: Long-distance craft sank at the front, taking sailors with it

indicators.note: the front of sank is its first letter

parts.note: tars is a traditional word for sailors
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A ship went down bow first, carrying its crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' looks like 'along with it' but means fashionable, HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a spacecraft for interstellar travel, the ultimate long-distance vessel.

clue.text: Bad thing the head of a certain police department did?

parts.note: what a head of a department does is run it, so the past thing the head did is ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: The chief of a police unit did something wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RAN CID: what the head of a police department did was run the CID, the plain-clothes detective branch of a British force. 'did' completes that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid means smelling or tasting of stale fat, so gone bad, off.

clue.text: One giant, messy denial

indicators.note: a mess of letters is a jumble, so one giant is rearranged

explanation.surface: A single giant gives an untidy refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of denying or contradicting something, a denial.

clue.text: Daughter has strange time getting tattoo

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a beat is a unit of musical time

explanation.surface: A daughter goes through an odd phase when she gets a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' looks like ink on skin but here is a drumming signal; RUM is British for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic tapping or drum signal, such as one recalling soldiers to quarters: a drumbeat.

clue.text: Old actor steals papers revealing the timing of a Shakespeare play

definitions.text: the timing of a Shakespeare play

indicators.note: a thief takes the goods in, so the papers end up inside the actor

parts.note: a mummer is an actor in a traditional folk play
IDs are identity papers

explanation.surface: A veteran performer pinches documents that expose when a Shakespeare play happens.
explanation.walkthrough: A mummer performed in traditional English folk plays at Christmas; 'papers' are identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midsummer Night's Dream is set on midsummer's eve, so midsummer is when that play happens.

clue.text: Excellent medicine fixed up with a strong drink

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: rare can mean unusually good, excellent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Superb medicine mixed with a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'fixed up' means the letters read upwards; 'fixed' alone looks like an anagram signal but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara rum is a strong dark rum from Guyana, named after the Demerara river.

clue.text: Union-related crimes involving great female friends abroad?

parts.note: big means great or large
amies is French for female friends

explanation.surface: Offences tied to a trade union, implicating close female friends overseas?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests trade unions but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is the crime of marrying while already married, a crime of the marriage union.

clue.text: Grand chat about, for example, a rising emotional burden?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
gab is idle chat

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: A long talk about a growing emotional weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses G GAB into BAGG; 'rising' turns EG A into AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional baggage is a figurative load of past experiences one carries around, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Senior writer rebuffed rubbish, incomplete concept

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a concept

explanation.surface: A senior author turned down nonsense and a half-formed idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts IDEA to IDE; 'rebuffed' reverses ROT IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist in charge of a publication or section.

clue.text: Having no lead, gendarme awkwardly called again

indicators.note: awkwardly arranged letters are put in a clumsy new order
the lead of a word is its first letter, here dropped from gendarme

explanation.surface: Without leadership, a policeman was clumsily re-titled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no lead' drops G, and 'awkwardly' rearranges ENDARME.
explanation.definitionFit: Renamed means given a new name, so called by another name again.

clue.text: Attend religious area with Democrat, get exhausted

parts.note: to go to an event is to attend it
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: Go to church with a Democrat and become worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that goes to seed has passed its best, so figuratively to go to seed is to run down, become worn out.

clue.text: Info obtained from small markings on the skin

parts.note: tats is slang for tattoos

explanation.surface: Data gleaned from little tattoos.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats, short for statistics, are figures and data, informal information.

clue.text: Departs from a city somewhere in South Africa

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
urban means of or from a city

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a city for a place in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a major port city in KwaZulu-Natal province, South Africa.

clue.text: Bishop reportedly also comprehends a number of foreign languages

indicators.note: comprehends means contains, so the a and the number sit within

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard, so too is represented by letters sounding the same

parts.note: too means also
N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A bishop is said also to understand several foreign tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns TOO into TU; B plus TU 'comprehends' A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of related languages spoken across central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Slough is quiet and expected to be evacuated

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: a word evacuated has its inside emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Berkshire town is calm and due to be emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the town west of London but is the verb to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough skin is to cast it off, exactly what to shed means.

clue.text: In first place, although really only maybe by a nose

indicators.note: in first place points to the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A winner by only the narrowest margin, a nose ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a nose' looks like a racing phrase, but 'nose' is the definition and A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose is a wine-taster's word for a wine's smell or bouquet.

clue.text: Attacking an opponent's character made him no different

indicators.note: made different means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insult to his character left him no different.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad hominem argument targets the person rather than their case, a personal attack.

clue.text: Wait and offer to buy everyone a pint?

definitions.text: offer to buy everyone a pint?
definitions.meaning: to ... is to pay for drinks for the whole group

explanation.surface: Hang about and get the drinks in for the whole pub?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as STAND A ROUND: in British pubs one person buys a round of drinks for the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing around is idle waiting, while standing a round is treating everyone to drinks.
